title: An Optimized Convolutional Neural Network Framework for Cancer Classification Using RNA-Seq Transformation.
abstract: Inspired by the hierarchical, receptive-field-based processing of biological vision and by synaptic pruning in the developing brain, this work proposes a bio-inspired optimized convolutional neural network framework for multi-class cancer classification from RNA-Seq gene expression data. Although current deep learning models achieve strong predictive performance, existing approaches typically rely either on large pre-trained networks that cannot be deployed on resource-constrained devices or on image representations that normalize gene expression values to the 8-bit range (0-255), discarding the original biological dynamic range. A variance-driven feature selection step reduces 20,531 gene profiles to 16,384 high-information features, which are then reshaped into 128 × 128 images while preserving the original log2-normalized expression range (approximately 0-20.78) without rescaling to that 8-bit range. The network architecture is derived from a parametric mathematical model that enables analytical control over parameter count and FLOPs, resulting in a compact network with only 0.16 million parameters, a model size of 1.29 MB, and 0.0372 GFLOPs. On the TCGA PANCAN dataset (five cancer classes), the proposed baseline achieves 99.38% accuracy, matching or exceeding twelve state-of-the-art pre-trained architectures. For real-world deployment, the network was further optimized through two pathways: (A) direct TensorFlow Lite quantization in FP32, FP16, and INT8, and (B) structured channel pruning, analogous to synaptic pruning, followed by TFLite conversion. All variants retained the baseline 99.38% accuracy, with the Pruned TFLite FP16 variant reducing computational cost by 23.4% to 0.0285 GFLOPs, model size by 80.6%, and latency by 75.4%, while achieving the highest throughput of 1256 images/s at only 0.25 MB.

title: Quality of Life, Social Support, and Spiritual Well-Being in Tanzanian Women with Cervical Cancer: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Social support and spiritual well-being may matter for the quality of life (QoL) of women with cervical cancer in sub-Saharan Africa, but their interrelations are rarely studied. This study examined their associations with QoL in Tanzanian women. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 499 women recruited consecutively at two Tanzanian cancer centers completed the EORTC QLQ-C30, the EORTC QLQ-SWB32 and a Kiswahili ENRICHD Social Support Instrument (ESSI). Associations were examined using multivariable regression and mediation analysis. Results: In adjusted regression (n = 460), higher social support (B = 0.80 per ESSI point, 95% CI 0.49-1.11) and higher global spiritual well-being (B = 0.11, 95% CI 0.04-0.17) were associated with higher global QoL. The statistical indirect association via spiritual well-being was small (ab = 0.19, 95% CI 0.05-0.34; 19.2% of the total association) and robust to multiple imputation and additional covariates, but it was present at only one center (difference -0.42, 95% CI -0.78 to -0.06) and could not be distinguished from reverse orderings. Neither variable was positively associated with the QLQ-C30 summary score. Conclusions: Both social support and spiritual well-being were associated with women's global appraisal of QoL rather than with functioning or symptoms; longitudinal studies are needed to establish direction and clinical relevance.

title: Phelan-McDermid Syndrome in a 4-Year-Old Girl: A Case Report.
abstract: Phelan-McDermid syndrome (PMS; OMIM #606232) is a rare genetic disorder caused by terminal or interstitial deletions involving chromosome 22q13 or by pathogenic variants in the SHANK3 gene, which plays a critical role in synaptic function and neurodevelopment. PMS is characterized by marked clinical heterogeneity, with core manifestations including neonatal hypotonia, intellectual disability, severe speech impairment, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder. We report the case of a 4-year-old girl presenting with intellectual disability, severe speech delay, and craniofacial dysmorphism. Cytogenetic and molecular cytogenetic analyses identified a ring chromosome 22, with variation in SHANK3 signal loss across tissues and retention of the 22q subtelomeric probe. This case highlights the importance of early genetic diagnosis for the timely identification of associated comorbidities and the initiation of multidisciplinary rehabilitation and developmental interventions, ultimately improving long-term functional outcomes and quality of life.

title: Argonaute 2 in the Nervous System: Where Causality Is Established in Neurodevelopment and Only Inferred in Neurodegeneration.
abstract: The RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC), built around the Argonaute proteins, executes microRNA-mediated gene silencing. AGO2, the only catalytically active human paralogue, stabilises mature microRNAs in neurons and controls local translation in dendrites and axons. AGO2 is now invoked across the whole span of neurological disease, from monogenic neurodevelopmental syndromes to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, on evidence of very unequal strength. We therefore ask of each body of work two questions: what was experimentally manipulated, and what was then measured. De novo variants in AGO1 and AGO2 cause the Argonaute syndromes, where the mechanism has been traced from the kinetics of the mutant protein to knock-in mouse phenotypes and indicates delayed strand release rather than loss of function; conditional Ago2 deletion in mice is comparably direct for neurovascular development and adult neurogenesis. In neurodegenerative disease, the position differs. The DISE mechanism shows that AGO2 activity sets the threshold for amyloid-beta toxicity in cultured neurons, and one study identifies AGO2 as an endogenous brake on alpha-synuclein synthesis, but no experiment has yet tested whether altering AGO2 in vivo changes neurodegeneration, even though deleting the upstream enzyme Dicer kills dopaminergic neurons. Benchmarked against TDP-43-dependent mis-splicing, where causality in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is established, AGO2 remains a convergence point for several pathological processes rather than a demonstrated driver of any of them. The available evidence neither establishes nor excludes a causal role, and we set out the experiments that would decide.

title: Acute Intestinal Infections in Children Aged 1-5 in Developed and Developing Countries.
abstract: Acute intestinal infections remain one of the leading causes of morbidity among children under five years of age and represent an important public health challenge in both developed and developing countries. Although these infections often share similar clinical manifestations, their etiological structure, severity, diagnostic accessibility, treatment approaches, and prevention strategies differ considerably depending on socioeconomic conditions, sanitation, healthcare infrastructure, and vaccination coverage. This review aims to summarize current data on the epidemiology, etiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of acute intestinal infections in children aged 1-5 years, as well as to provide a comparative analysis of approaches in countries with different income levels. A review of scientific literature focused on acute intestinal infections in young children was conducted. Source selection included full-text assessment. The extracted data were summarized descriptively according to pathogen groups: viral, bacterial, and protozoal infections. A PRISMA flow diagram was used to present the source selection process. The reviewed literature indicates that viral pathogens, particularly rotavirus and norovirus, are among the leading causes of acute gastroenteritis in children under five years of age. According to Global Burden of Disease 2021 estimates, approximately 392.8 million diarrhoeal episodes and 0.34 million deaths occurred among children under five years of age globally in 2021, with mortality disproportionately concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Bacterial infections, including Shigella and diarrheagenic Escherichia coli, are less frequent but are more often associated with invasive disease, severe diarrhea, and systemic complications. Protozoal infections, including Giardia lamblia, may contribute to prolonged diarrhea, especially in children with malnutrition or weakened immune status. Substantial regional differences were identified in pathogen distribution, antimicrobial resistance, diagnostic capacity, access to healthcare, and vaccination coverage. In developing countries, the disease burden remains strongly associated with limited access to safe water, sanitation, timely diagnosis, and appropriate medical care, whereas in developed countries acute intestinal infections more commonly contribute to outbreaks, emergency department visits, and hospitalizations. Acute intestinal infections in children aged 1-5 years remain an important global health burden with substantial regional disparities. Effective prevention and control require context-specific strategies combining high vaccination coverage, improved water, sanitation and hygiene, timely pathogen-specific diagnosis, rational antimicrobial use, and strengthened surveillance, with particular priority given to high-burden and resource-limited settings.

title: Evaluation of Sensing Properties of Defective and Zn-Doped MoS2 Monolayers for Cortisol, Epinephrine, and Norepinephrine Detection: A DFT Study.
abstract: Accurate quantification of the major stress hormones cortisol, epinephrine, and norepinephrine supports the detection and prevention of cardiovascular, metabolic, and neuropsychiatric disorders. This study examines the sensitivity of a MoS2 monolayer-based sensing system to these hormones. Quantum mechanical calculations were used to investigate the interactions of cortisol, epinephrine, and norepinephrine with sulfur-vacancy-containing (MoS2-VS) and Zn-doped (Zn-MoS2) molybdenum disulfide monolayers. Adsorption energies, adsorption distances, charge transfer, work functions, and band gaps were evaluated for the investigated systems. All three molecules exhibited energetically favorable adsorption on the modified MoS2 monolayers, as indicated by negative adsorption energies. The strongest interactions were observed for the Zn-MoS2-cortisol and Zn-MoS2-norepinephrine systems, with Zn incorporation enhancing adsorption. The catecholamines, epinephrine and norepinephrine, exhibited greater charge transfer than cortisol. The largest charge transfer, +0.166e, was obtained for the Zn-MoS2-epinephrine system. Analysis of the electronic properties showed that molecular adsorption altered the work functions and band gaps of the systems. The largest work function change occurred in the MoS2-VS-norepinephrine system, while the largest band gap change was observed for Zn-MoS2-epinephrine. These results suggest that defective and Zn-doped MoS2 monolayers are highly sensitive to stress hormones and neurotransmitters. Sulfur vacancies yielded a stronger electronic response, reflected in changes in the work function and band structure. Zn doping strengthened adsorption and enhanced molecule-surface interactions. These findings highlight the potential of MoS2-VS for sensors based on work function changes and Zn-MoS2 for resistive biosensors for detecting cortisol, epinephrine, and norepinephrine.

title: Flexible Nano-Platinum Microelectrode Arrays for Sensitive and Spatially Resolved Nitric Oxide Monitoring.
abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) regulates neuronal signaling and neurovascular function, but its rapid diffusion, short lifetime, and reactivity complicate real-time detection in tissue. We developed flexible platinum microelectrode arrays (MEAs) modified with nanostructured platinum (nano-Pt) and a permselective poly(m-phenylenediamine) (mPD) coating for sensitive, selective NO monitoring. Nano-Pt electrodeposition reduced impedance approximately eightfold at 10 Hz and increased charge-storage capacity approximately 7.4-fold without increasing electrode dimensions. Simultaneous amperometric recordings from multiple electrode channels demonstrated the multisite sensing proof of concept of the flexible MEA platform. Amperometric calibration showed linear responses from 50 to 250 nM (R2 > 0.999), with a sensitivity of 243.16 ± 6.12 pA/µM and an operational detection limit of 50 nM. The mPD coating attenuated responses to ascorbic acid, uric acid, and dopamine. Sensors retained NO sensitivity (180 ± 8.6 pA/µM) in endothelial cell culture medium and detected transients following exposure of primary brain microvascular endothelial cells to copper-containing high-aspect-ratio structures (CuHARS), corresponding to peak NO-equivalent concentrations of 320 ± 50 nM. In mouse hippocampus, local NMDA/glycine administration evoked responses corresponding to estimated NO concentrations of 154 ± 31 nM. Finite-element simulations predicted detectable NO concentration gradients across neighboring electrode sites. These results support flexible nano-Pt/mPD MEAs for NO monitoring in complex biological environments and motivate experimental validation of spatially resolved measurements.

title: Fit-Derived Phasor Analysis of Metabolic Signatures of Cerebral Endothelial Dysfunction in Alzheimer's Disease: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
abstract: Vascular dysfunction at the level of cerebral endothelial cells is an early component of Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis. Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) with phasor analysis enables label-free assessment of cellular metabolism based on NAD(P)H autofluorescence. This proof-of-concept study aimed to evaluate the potential of FLIM with fit-derived phasor analysis to compare cerebral endothelial cells (CECs) derived from a healthy donor and a patient with Alzheimer's disease (AD) and to characterize their responses to metabolic modulators. CECs were differentiated from induced pluripotent stem cells obtained from a healthy donor (PO2) and a patient with AD (Alz9L, APP V717I mutation). Two-photon NAD(P)H FLIM was performed under basal conditions and following treatment with 3-chloro-5-hydroxybenzoic acid (3CLBA) and sodium lactate. The analysis included mean lifetime (τmean), phase lifetime (τφ), biexponential fitting parameters, and phasor coordinates reconstructed from these parameters. Under basal conditions, the phasor distributions of PO2 and Alz9L cells differed significantly despite similar mean NAD(P)H lifetimes. Alz9L cells exhibited a lower τφ and a higher lifetime of the short-lived component, τ1. Following sodium lactate treatment, Alz9L cells exhibited a higher a1/a2 ratio and lower τmean and τ1 values than PO2 cells. Comparison of the basal and post-lactate states revealed pronounced decreases in τmean and τ1 in Alz9L cells. Fit-derived phasor analysis jointly visualizes fitted NAD(P)H decay parameters and illustrates differences between the two studied CEC lines despite similar basal mean lifetimes. These proof-of-concept observations require validation in additional cell lines from independent donors.

title: Supramolecular Complexation of BeRST for Live-Cell Voltage Imaging.
abstract: Voltage-sensitive fluorescent dyes enable optical measurements of transmembrane potential but can be limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation, and incomplete cellular membrane loading. Here, we evaluated supramolecular complexation as an approach to improve the imaging performance of the voltage-sensitive fluorophore Berkeley Red Sensor of Transmembrane potential (BeRST). BeRST was complexed with bovine serum albumin (BSA) and structurally distinct cyclodextrins (CDs), and its solution-phase photophysical properties and live-cell fluorescence intensity were assessed. Both host identity and concentration influenced the local environment of the BeRST chromophore, producing spectral changes consistent with reduced aggregation. In HEK 293T cells, the effects of complexation on mean cellular fluorescence intensity were likewise host- and concentration-dependent, with all hosts evaluated significantly enhancing mean cellular fluorescence intensity under at least one condition. The voltage sensitivity of complexed BeRST in live cells remains unchanged from noncomplexed BeRST, as determined by voltage imaging. Together, these findings show that CD complexation can tune the photophysical and cellular imaging properties of BeRST while preserving its voltage sensitivity, supporting supramolecular complexation as a strategy to improve the delivery and cellular brightness of lipophilic voltage-sensitive fluorescent dyes.

title: Optimizing Molecular Profiling for Decision-Making in mCRPC: Integrating Tissue Biopsy, Liquid Biopsy and Re-Biopsy Through a Broad Multidisciplinary Approach.
abstract: Molecular profiling is essential for therapeutic decision-making in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), but implementation is limited by tissue availability, bone-predominant disease, tumor heterogeneity and organizational barriers. This conference report summarizes a multidisciplinary educational meeting held in Naples, Italy, on 12 May 2026. The program combined presentations, moderated multidisciplinary discussions and two exploratory audience polls addressing nine questions. Survey results were summarized descriptively to contextualize the discussion. Molecular profiling was viewed as an integrated diagnostic pathway rather than an isolated laboratory test. Successful implementation requires timely planning, involvement of interventional radiologists in the multidisciplinary selection among nodal, visceral, osseous and other metastatic biopsy targets, optimized tissue acquisition and processing, early pathological assessment of specimen adequacy and coordinated interpretation of molecular findings. Archival tissue, newly acquired metastatic tissue, liquid biopsy and re-biopsy were considered complementary strategies to optimize profiling according to disease characteristics, specimen availability, prior results and clinical needs. Non-informative results should prompt reassessment and consideration of an alternative sampling strategy, consistent with diagnostic persistence. Implementation depends on multidisciplinary collaboration and adaptable pathways addressing access, geographic equity and resource sustainability. This evidence-informed framework aims to support harmonization of molecular profiling pathways in mCRPC without yet constituting recommendations or formal consensus.

title: Anatomical Proximity Between the Retromolar Canal and Mandibular Third Molars on Cone-Beam CT: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The retromolar canal (RMC) and retromolar foramen (RMF) are anatomical variations in the posterior mandible that may lie close to mandibular third molars and may contain neurovascular structures. This study aimed to characterize RMC/RMF-third-molar proximity on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), with close proximity defined a priori as a minimum distance < 2 mm. Methods: This retrospective CBCT study included 100 adults (200 hemimandibles). RMC/RMF morphology and morphometry, Pell and Gregory class and position, and Winter angulation were assessed. Generalized estimating equations accounted for within-patient clustering, and inter-observer reliability was quantified. Results: RMCs were identified in 41/200 hemimandibles (20.5%; patient-clustered 95% CI, 14.9-27.6%) and 32/100 patients (32.0%; 95% CI, 23.7-41.7%). Among RMC-positive hemimandibles that also contained a third molar (n = 26), 8 showed a minimum RMC/RMF-third-molar distance < 2 mm (30.8%; patient-clustered 95% CI, 14.9-52.9%). When all hemimandibles containing a third molar were considered (n = 121), the same close-proximity configuration was present in 8 (6.6%). No statistically significant association was detected between RMC presence and third-molar presence, Pell and Gregory class or position, or Winter angulation. Inter-observer agreement was high (κ = 0.757-0.951; ICC = 0.960-0.995). Conclusions: Close RMC/RMF-third-molar proximity occurred in a substantial subset of RMC-positive sites, although precision was limited. The findings suggest that direct assessment of the RMC/RMF may offer complementary anatomical information beyond conventional impaction classifications; this hypothesis requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

title: Clinical Efficacy of a Chlorhexidine-Based Mouthrinse Containing Citrox (Citrus Aurantium Amara Extract) and Hyaluronic Acid in Early Wound Healing of Patients Undergoing Periodontal Surgery: A Triple-Blind, Parallel-Arm, Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background: Chlorhexidine (CHX) is the reference chemical plaque control agent used after periodontal surgery, but higher concentrations are associated with adverse effects that can reduce patient compliance. This randomized controlled trial evaluated whether a mouthrinse combining a reduced CHX concentration (0.09%) with Citrox and hyaluronic acid (HA) could match the clinical performance of conventional 0.12% CHX after periodontal flap surgery, while improving tolerability. Methods: Thirty-two patients undergoing open flap debridement with an experimental vertical releasing incision randomly received a mouthrinse containing 0.09% CHX with Citrox and HA (TEST group) or conventional 0.12% CHX (CONTROL group) twice daily for 14 days. The primary outcome was the presence of edema; secondary outcomes were the Early Wound Healing Score (EHS) and its components, the plaque index (TQHPI), the gingival index (GI), the tooth/tongue staining index (SI), and the adverse events of oral ulcers and dysgeusia, assessed at baseline and at 3, 7, and 14 days. Results: Edema, EHS, and the GI did not differ significantly between the groups at any time point (edema at day 3: 37.5% in both groups; risk difference 0.0%; 95% CI -30.5% to 30.5%). The plaque index was significantly higher in the TEST group from day 7 (p = 0.003; median difference 0.20, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.40) to day 14 (p = 0.005; median difference 0.30, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.40). The distribution of staining scores differed significantly at day 14 (p = 0.008), with heavy staining observed only in the control group. Conclusions: No statistically significant differences between the reduced-concentration, multi-component mouthrinse, and 0.12% CHX were detected in the assessed wound-healing outcomes; the test formulation was associated with higher plaque scores from day 7 and with a different distribution of staining scores at day 14, without heavy staining. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger trials.

title: Addenbrooke Cognitive Examination-III Performance Reflects Dementia Severity More Than Diagnostic Subtype in Late-Onset Alzheimer Disease and Mixed Dementia.
abstract: To determine whether Addenbrooks Cognitive Examination-III (ACE-III) performance differentiates late-onset Alzheimer disease (AD) from mixed dementia (MD) or primarily reflects dementia severity. The study included individuals aged 65 years and older diagnosed with either probable AD or MD according to established clinical criteria. Dementia severity ranged from mild to moderately severe stages. Data from 1013 patients with dementia (AD: n=631; MD: n=382) were analyzed. General linear models examined associations between diagnosis and ACE-III performance after adjustment for age, sex, education, and dementia severity. Partial R2 values quantified the variance explained by diagnosis and severity. Compared with AD, MD was associated with better Memory but lower Fluency and Visuospatial domains scores. After adjustment, diagnosis did not independently predict ACE-III total score (β=1.12, 95% CI: -0.10 to 2.33, P=0.072). Dementia severity was the strongest determinant of performance, explaining 28.0% of the variance in ACE-III total score (partial R2=0.280), whereas diagnosis explained 0.3% (partial R2=0.003). Memory showed the largest domain-level difference between groups. ACE-III performance is influenced predominantly by dementia severity rather than diagnostic subtype. Although modest domain-level differences exist between AD and MD, global ACE-III scores appear more useful for staging dementia severity than for differential diagnosis.

title: Spatial Mismatch Between Structural Progression and Mean Microperimetry Sensitivity in Choroideremia.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the relationship between structural progression metrics and functional decline measured by microperimetry (MP) in choroideremia (CHM). This post hoc retrospective analysis included 99 eyes from the Natural History of the Progression of Choroideremia Study (NIGHT) with available baseline and 12-month fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging and MP data. Residual retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) area, square root transformed area, and mean preserved autofluorescence border (PAF-B) displacement, defined as the average change in border position from baseline to month 12 across 12 clock-hour sectors, were quantified using FAF-based binary mask analysis. Correlations between changes in MP mean sensitivity and structural parameters were evaluated using Pearson correlation analysis. PAF area significantly decreased from baseline to month 12 (3.23 ± 4.19 mm² vs. 2.90 ± 3.90 mm², P < 0.001). The square-root transformed area and MP mean sensitivity also showed significant declines over time (both P < 0.01). Annualized PAF-B displacement demonstrated significant regression (-0.10 ± 0.20 mm/year, P < 0.001). However, no significant correlations were observed between MP sensitivity change and raw area change (r = 0.095, P = 0.35), square root transformed area change (r = 0.015, P = 0.88), or PAF-B displacement (r = 0.122, P = 0.23). Conventional structural progression metrics in CHM were not significantly associated with MP mean sensitivity decline. These findings suggest that mean MP sensitivity may not adequately reflect structural progression and highlight the need for novel functional assessment approaches which incorporate spatial characteristics of the disease. A spatial mismatch between structural progression and mean MP sensitivity may limit the utility of mean sensitivity as a functional outcome measure in CHM.

title: Gastric resection versus clip-based gastroplasty differentially modulates neuroendocrine and metabolic responses in obese mice.
abstract: Sleeve gastrectomy (SG) and non-resection, restrictive gastric procedures are increasingly used to treat severe obesity, yet the relative contributions of gastric resection versus pure restriction to metabolic remodeling remain unclear. To mechanistically dissect these components, diet-induced obese male C57BL/6J mice were randomized to either SG or a surgically clip-based sleeve gastroplasty (GP) model that narrows the gastric body without resection, or sham surgery, and longitudinally phenotyped for body weight, energy balance, glucose homeostasis, lipid metabolism, gut hormones, hypothalamic neuropeptide expression, and circulating branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs). SG and clip-based GP produced comparable weight loss over six weeks (12% and 11%, respectively). Despite similar energy expenditure, the two procedures showed distinct temporal patterns of hypophagia, with SG uniquely altering feeding microstructure. SG, but not GP, improved glucose tolerance and reduced hepatic triglyceride content in a weight-independent manner, accompanied by a selective reduction in plasma BCAAs. Hypothalamic analyses revealed reduced POMC after both interventions, whereas NPY and AgRP were selectively suppressed after SG, indicating resection-specific modulation of central orexigenic pathways. SG also elicited a more pronounced endorcine response with higher glucose-stimulated glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide, amylin, C-peptide, insulin, glucagon, and peptide-YY. Together, these findings show that gastric resection confers additional neuroendocrine and metabolic benefits beyond those achieved by non-resection gastric restriction alone.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals sex-specific microglial responses to simulated galactic cosmic radiation without broad inflammatory activation.
abstract: Long‑duration deep space missions expose astronauts to galactic cosmic radiation (GCR), a complex mixture of high‑ and low‑LET ions that can compromise central nervous system (CNS) health. Microglia, the resident immune cells of the brain, are highly sensitive to radiation, yet their cell‑state adaptations to space‑relevant mixed‑field exposure remain poorly defined. Here, we performed single‑cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of hippocampal and cortical microglia isolated from male and female C57BL/6 J mice 53 days after acute 100 cGy 5‑ion simulated GCR (GCRsim). Behavioral testing showed no overt deficits, but scRNA‑seq revealed subtle, sex‑specific transcriptional remodeling. Male microglia engaged a stress‑adaptive program characterized by upregulation of Fkbp5, Ddit4, Adrb1, and metabolic regulators, with concurrent downregulation of ER chaperone genes. Female microglia displayed a transcriptionally blunted phenotype with selective induction of Fkbp5, Ccnd3, Tsc22d3 and Tnfaip2, and broad downregulation of inflammatory and Nucleotide-binding Oligomerization Domain (NOD)/Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF) pathways. Notably, canonical inflammatory or disease‑associated microglia (DAM) signatures were absent, and homeostatic markers (P2ry12, Cx3cr1) were preserved. FKBP5 immunoreactivity within Iba1 + microglia was significantly increased in both the dentate gyrus and cortex after GCRsim, without any change in total microglial volume. These findings define a non‑inflammatory, sex‑specific microglial response to space‑relevant GCR. This refined understanding of microglial adaptation provides a cellular framework for sex‑informed CNS risk assessment and countermeasure development for deep space travel.

title: Predictive functional network connectivity signature of infancy age and eye-region fixation behavior.
abstract: Functional connectivity (FC) has been established as a fundamental property of brain organization, intricately linked to both neurodevelopmental processes and the emergence of social behavior. Prior research has demonstrated that individual variability in brain age is associated with cognitive performance, primarily through the architecture of brain networks, underscoring the predictive ability of FC to characterize brain maturation. However, most existing work has focused on later developmental stages across the lifespan, with comparatively limited attention to early infancy-a period marked by rapid neurobiological growth and the emergence of foundational social skills. In this study, we applied an independent component analysis (ICA) framework to resting-state fMRI data from a longitudinal infant cohort, spanning from birth to 8 months of age, to characterize functional network connectivity (FNC). Using a linear mixed-effects model, we identified widespread but spatially heterogeneous associations between FNC and chronological age (maximum r = 0.6420, FDR-corrected p < 0.05), indicating region-specific developmental trajectories. To further model multivariate patterns of neurodevelopment, we employed partial least squares regression (PLSR) to predict brain age from whole-brain FNC. The model demonstrated high predictive accuracy (r = 0.8704, permutation test p < 1.0 × 10⁻3), confirming the feasibility of connectome-based brain age estimation in early infancy. Predictive performance remained robust in a subset of infants identified as low likelihood for autism spectrum disorder (r = 0.8713, permutation test p < 1.0 × 10⁻3). A model incorporating gestational age (i.e., corrected age) showed similarly significant performance (r = 0.8902, permutation test p < 1.0 × 10⁻3) and yielded a modest but significant improvement in accuracy (two-sample t-test p = 2.57 × 10⁻153), highlighting the importance of perinatal timing in neurodevelopmental modeling. In addition to brain age, FNC also predicted individual differences in early social attention, specifically fixation to the eyes (r = 0.4684) and mouth (r = 0.4687), with both associations reaching statistical significance (p < 1.0 × 10⁻3). Notably, predictive maps for eye and mouth fixation exhibited a robust inverse correlation (r = -0.5016, p = 2.08 × 10⁻145), suggesting that attentional allocation toward these socially salient features may be driven by distinct and potentially antagonistic patterns of brain network organization, implicating early adaptive social signaling mechanisms. Collectively, these findings suggest that resting-state FC, combined with multivariate modeling approaches, may capture meaningful associations with individual differences in brain maturation and early social behavior during infancy. The present work highlights the potential utility of functional connectome-based frameworks for studying early neurodevelopmental variability and characterizing developmental processes during critical periods of brain maturation.

title: Mutation E300 recommended by protein language models gives ChrimsonR amplified photocurrent response.
abstract: A central challenge in rhodopsin engineering is identifying mutations that reliably improve desired functional properties, a task made difficult by the enormous mutation space and limited throughput of electrophysiological screening. Improving rhodopsin properties such as photocurrent amplitude and light sensitivity have the potential to broaden the use of rhodopsins to low-light and deep-tissue applications. With this goal, we applied zero-shot protein language models (ESM-1b/1v) to recommend ChrimsonR mutations and experimentally validated all 17 of these variants using whole-cell patch clamp electrophysiology (n=6 cells per mutation). Despite many mutations reducing function, protein language models identified both known functional residues and unconventional substitutions that produced large functional gains and synergized with K176R to accelerate channel closing. Two mutations, E300G and E300P, increased sustained photocurrents from 66 pA (control) to 305 pA and 255 pA at 635 nm, reduced [Formula: see text] at 575 nm from 0.19 mW to 0.07 mW, and altered kinetics ([Formula: see text] increased from 0.06 s up to 0.40 s relative to ChrimsonR). Our results suggest that protein language models, even without task-specific training, can be used alongside electrophysiological measurements as a strategy for screening rhodopsins for enhanced photocurrent.

title: Expected reward value and reward prediction errors reinforce but also interfere with human time perception.
abstract: Time perception is often investigated using instrumental paradigms where reinforcement learning and associated dopaminergic processes have modulatory effects. Interval timing, which includes the judgment of relatively short intervals of time (ranging from milliseconds to minutes), has been shown to be modulated by manipulations of striatal dopamine. In reinforcement learning theory, the 'expected value of reward' (EV) and 'reward prediction errors' (RPEs) are key variables that explain striatal dopaminergic signals of reward processing during instrumental learning. Despite potential common dopaminergic underpinnings, the underlying connection between reinforcement learning processes and interval timing remains relatively underexplored. Herein, we investigated the impact of EV and RPEs on the human reproduction of 1000ms, 3000ms, and 5000ms intervals of time. Our results demonstrate that RPEs - specifically about rewards and not punishments - appear to reinforce performance errors, which effectively interfere with the rate at which reinforced 1000ms intervals - but not 3000ms and 5000ms intervals - are learned. The results of these experiments help clarify the role reinforcements play in interval timing, as well as give insight into the hypothetical mechanisms underlying time perception and the potential shared relationship with reinforcement learning processes.

title: Associations of High Blood Pressure with Brain Network Functional Connectivity in Healthy Young Adults.
abstract: Higher blood pressure (BP) in middle-aged and older adults is associated with altered brain network functional connectivity (FC), but evidence in young adults is limited. This study explored the associations of BP with brain FC in healthy young adults. This cross-sectional study included 1,000 young adults (53.8% women, 22-37 years) from the Human Connectome Project, with no hypertension diagnosis or antihypertensive medication use. Brachial systolic (SBP) and diastolic BP (DBP) were measured using semi-automatic or manual sphygmomanometer. Resting-state functional MRI measured FC within the default-mode (DMN), frontoparietal control (FPN), dorsal attention (DAN), salience/ventral attention (SVN), limbic (LN), somatomotor (SMN), and visual (VN) networks. Linear regression examined associations of SBP and DBP with network FC, adjusting for age, sex, education, body mass index (BMI), smoking history, and alcohol consumption. Mean (±SD) SBP and DBP were 123.3 ± 13.8 and 76.3 ± 10.5 mmHg. Per 10-mm Hg higher SBP, FC was lower in the SVN (B = -0.0030, 95% CI: -0.0050 to - 0.0010) and higher in the DAN (B = 0.0070, 95% CI: 0.0030 to 0.0100). Per 10-mm Hg higher DBP, FC was lower in the DMN (B = -0.0040, 95% CI: -0.0060 to - 0.0010), SVN (B = -0.0050, 95% CI: -0.0070 to - 0.0020), LN (B = -0.0040, 95% CI: -0.0080 to - 0.0010), SMN (B = -0.0030, 95% CI: -0.0060 to - 0.0005), and higher in the DAN (B = 0.0070; 95% CI, 0.0010 to 0.0100). Higher BP is associated with altered brain network FC in early adulthood.

title: Skin-like Prototissues Integrating Pro-Angiogenic Signaling with Antibacterial Barrier Function.
abstract: The bottom-up assembly of prototissues from synthetic protocells provides a promising route for bridging artificial cell engineering with tissue-level functionality; however, integrating biochemical signaling with adaptive barrier properties within such systems remains challenging. Here, we construct skin-like prototissues by embedding catalytically active coacervate vesicle protocells within a gelatin-hydroxypropyltrimethylammonium chloride chitosan hydrogel. Within this architecture, spatially organized protocells act as confined microreactors that convert endogenous glucose into nitric oxide (NO), establishing a self-sustained pro-angiogenic NO signaling cascade. Concurrently, evaporation-driven surface reorganization generates an epidermis-like hydrophobic interface with antibacterial barrier function. The integration of protocell-mediated NO signaling with matrix-driven antibacterial barrier function yields emergent skin-like functionality. Leveraging this integrated design, the prototissues are configured as bioactive patches that markedly accelerate healing of bacterially infected diabetic wounds by promoting neovascularization while suppressing bacterial colonization. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for translating prototissue architectures into functional therapeutic interfaces.

title: Uncovering Hidden Attentional Inefficiencies in Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Survivors Using the NIH Cognition Toolbox.
abstract: Clinically significant cancer-related cognitive changes are well documented in survivorship, but findings on neurocognitive outcomes in pediatric populations remain inconclusive and often rely on broad normative classifications or subjective report. Identifying subtle cognitive changes is particularly important in children, where even mild inefficiencies may negatively affect academic performance and psychosocial functioning. To evaluate cognitive functioning in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) survivors 1-3 years after completing chemotherapy compared to healthy peers using standardized neuropsychological measures and to compare objective performance with self-reported cognition. Seventeen pediatric ALL survivors and 47 age-matched children without history of disease (CTL) between 5 and 17 years of age completed a self-report measure of cognitive functioning and NIH Toolbox objective sensory and cognitive subtests. Group differences were compared using t-tests and regression analyses adjusted for age and biological sex. Self-report did not differentiate groups; both groups scored within the norm. In contrast, objective testing revealed inefficiencies in attentional control among ALL survivors even when mean scores remained within normative limits, whereas measures of memory and auditory sensory processing did not distinguish groups. Findings suggest that pediatric ALL survivors experience subtle but measurable attentional deficiencies following chemotherapy, even when performance falls within normative ranges. These results indicate that reliance on normative cutoffs or self-report measures alone may underestimate cognitive difficulties associated with childhood cancer treatment. More sensitive approaches for detecting attentional difficulties may improve identification of treatment-related cognitive changes during survivorship.

title: γ-Aminobutyric Acid Enhances the Effectiveness of Rhizobium Y406 in Alleviating Salinity Stress and Promoting Growth of Soybean.
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: Soybean-rhizobia symbiosis is critical for yield and soil fertility, yet saline-alkali stress severely impairs nodulation and plant growth. γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) enhances stress tolerance, but whether GABA promotes rhizobial performance remains unclear. This study isolated a strain of rhizobium bacterium, Sinorhizobium alkalisoli Y406, from nodules of salt-tolerant wild soybean, which exhibits halo-alkaliphilic tolerance and possesses plant-growth-promoting traits; moreover, it significantly enhances soybean nodulation. GABA enhanced the growth, chemotaxis, and stress tolerance of Y406 under salt stress conditions. The coapplication further enhanced soybean growth by increasing antioxidant enzyme activities, improving the soil NPK content, and promoting rhizosphere microbial richness and diversity. This study demonstrates that the combined application of biostimulant and rhizobia effectively alleviates saline-alkali stress in soybean, offering a promising strategy for improving stress tolerance and promoting the sustainable utilization of marginal lands in soybean cultivation.

title: Biochemical Conversion of Organophosphate Pesticide to Paracetamol (Toxin to Drug): Exploring the Utility of Recombinant Organophosphorus Acid Anhydrolase Variant (OPAA-FL) Enzyme and Silver Nanoparticles Immobilized Chitosan Hydrogel Beads.
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: The extensive reliance on organophosphate (OP) pesticides in agriculture has resulted in significant contamination of soil and water. This study introduces a sequential biocatalytic-nanocatalytic approach for detoxifying ethyl paraoxon (EP), an OP compound, into paracetamol, a therapeutic drug. This process employs a recombinant organophosphorus acid anhydrolase-FL variant (OPAA-FL) enzyme that was expressed and purified from E. coli and conjugated to chitosan hydrogel beads that degraded 90.2% of EP from a concentration of 350 μM, yielding p-nitrophenol (PNP) within 30 min, while silver nanoparticles-embedded chitosan beads (AgCh) then reduced PNP to p-aminophenol (PAP) using AgCh in the presence of sodium borohydride (NaBH4), followed by acetylation of PAP to produce paracetamol. The product formation at each stage was validated using UV-visible spectroscopy, HPLC, and NMR, with comparisons to standard compounds. The integrated chemobiocatalytic method emphasizes a "waste-to-wealth" approach demonstrates a sustainable "waste-to-wealth" strategy, combining environmental detoxification with pharmaceutical synthesis through green circular bioprocessing.

title: Efficacy of Microvascular Decompression in Idiopathic Trigeminal Neuralgia (Without Vascular Compression): A Long-Term Cohort Study.
abstract: Trigeminal neuralgia (TN) is a severe facial pain disorder marked by brief, shock-like attacks along the trigeminal nerve distribution. The International Headache Society classifies TN into various subtypes; classical TN (cTN) results from neurovascular compression causing trigeminal nerve root atrophy or displacement, whereas idiopathic TN (iTN) presents without nerve compression or major morphological changes. Although microvascular decompression (MVD) is the first-line surgical treatment for cTN, its efficacy in iTN is poorly understood. Few studies have evaluated outcomes in patients strictly defined by the updated the International Headache Society criteria. This study aims to address these gaps by examining the long-term efficacy of MVD in patients with iTN and identifying predictors of pain freedom. In this retrospective cohort of patients with iTN, adjusted logistic regression evaluated factors associated with long-term MVD outcomes, including age, sex, efficacy of oxcarbazepine/carbamazepine, symptom duration before MVD, and neurovascular conflict. Between 2013 and 2022, 90 patients undergoing MVD for iTN were included with a median follow-up of 5.1 years (2.2-10.3). Outcomes were as follows: 52 (57.8%) were pain-free without mediation, 6 (6.7%) were pain-free with medication, 7 (7.7%) experienced partial relief, and 25 (27.8%) required subsequent procedures. Long-term outcomes were not significantly associated with age (P = .47), sex (P = .65), symptom duration (P = .19), or medication efficacy (P = .32). Arterial contact was associated with significantly better pain outcomes compared with no arterial contact (P = .037). Patients with iTN may still benefit from MVD, particularly when arterial contact is evident on preoperative imaging. Recognizing distinct iTN subtypes may improve individualized treatment strategies for TN and guide future studies.

title: One-Pot Assembly of Porphyrin-Gold Nanostructures with Enhanced Photothermal Response toward Biomedical Applications.
abstract: A simple aqueous one-pot strategy was developed for the direct preparation of gold-porphyrin nanoassemblies (AuNPs@por) using an amino-functionalized porphyrin as an active molecular building block. Unlike conventional postsynthetic conjugation approaches, the porphyrin contributed to nanoparticle organization during NaBH4-mediated reduction, enabling the rapid formation of hybrid nanostructures under mild conditions. Systematic variation of the reducing-agent amount showed that, whereas bare gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) displayed tunable size and surface characteristics, the presence of the porphyrin promoted their organization into compact, positively charged nanoassemblies with reproducible structural features. The optimized formulation exhibited long-term colloidal stability (>6 months), high porphyrin loading (30 ± 0.5 μmol g-1), and retention of the characteristic optical signature of the free-base porphyrin, confirming its effective incorporation while preserving its optical properties. The resulting proof-of-concept platform was readily biofunctionalized with PNA and DNA model probes through electrostatic interactions, preserving colloidal stability and molecular-recognition capability while improving hemocompatibility. Under 532 nm laser irradiation, AuNPs@por exhibited an enhanced photothermal response compared with bare AuNPs (ΔT up to 8.5 °C vs 3.2 °C). Furthermore, ex vivo irradiation of human oral squamous cell carcinoma tissue induced localized morphological alterations consistent with a predominantly photothermal effect, supporting the light-to-heat conversion capability of the hybrid nanoassemblies.

title: Configural grouping modulates memory attraction via feature-based perceptual unity in visual working memory.
abstract: Visual working memory representations of similar items are often systematically biased toward or away from neighbouring items. The present study examined how configural grouping via a Kanizsa illusory figure interacts with feature similarity to modulate these biases when task-irrelevant distractors are present. Both experiments employed a spatially interleaved layout, requiring participants to remember colour-similar targets while ignoring distractors. In Experiment 1, identically coloured distractors were either configured into a Kanizsa figure or remained ungrouped, with a no-distractor baseline. Configural grouping amplified target memory attraction toward the distractor colour and increased swap errors, without affecting d' (memory strength or clarity). In Experiment 2, grouping similarly coloured targets into a Kanizsa figure did not alter memory bias, swap rate, or d', regardless of distractor presence. Together, configural grouping intensified the influence of feature-homogeneous distractors on memory biases but provided no advantage for feature-heterogeneous targets. The asymmetry is consistent with the idea that, in interleaved layouts, grouping homogeneous distractors disrupts the coding of directional relationships between targets and distractors, increasing target-distractor confusion and attraction; whereas grouping heterogeneous targets does not appear to modify these relationships. Future research is needed to examine whether stronger competitive conditions could reveal target-grouping benefits.

title: Retinal Hyperreflective Foci (HRF) as a biomarker of microglial activation: Evidence across MS phenotypes and association with paramagnetic rim lesions.
abstract: Beyond optical coherence tomography (OCT) layer thickness, hyperreflective foci (HRF) may reflect retinal and cerebral microglial activation. Their role in primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS) remains unknown. We compared HRF across PPMS, early relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS), and HC, and assessed associations with paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs). This cross-sectional study prospectively recruited 97 participants: 51 early-RMS, 29 PPMS, and 17 HC. Patients had either a first multiple sclerosis (MS) event within 5 years or progressive symptoms for at least 5 years. Three blinded raters quantified GCIPL- and INL-HRF on OCT using published criteria. Eyes with optic neuritis were excluded. Groups were compared using ANOVA with Bonferroni correction. PRLs were assessed on MRI within 1 year, and associations were analysed using negative binomial regression. INL-HRF count was higher in PPMS and early-RMS than in HC (18.7, 18.2, and 13.4; p = 0.047 and 0.037), without differences between MS subtypes. GCIPL-HRF count did not differ. INL-HRF count discriminated MS from HC (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.708; threshold 15: 70% sensitivity, 65% specificity). HRF were unrelated to age, sex, disease duration, or PRL count. INL-HRF count was more frequent in MS than in HC but did not distinguish PPMS or higher PRL burden. Their utility may be limited by modest accuracy and time-consuming assessment.

title: Patient Satisfaction With Intravenous Conscious Sedation for Dental Treatment and Associated Factors: A Prospective Observational Study.
journal: Special care in dentistry : official publication of the American Association of Hospital Dentists, the Academy of Dentistry for the Handicapped, and the American Society for Geriatric Dentistry
abstract: To evaluate patient satisfaction with intravenous sedation during dental treatment and to identify clinical factors associated with lower satisfaction. This prospective observational study included patients who underwent intravenous sedation between August 2023 and March 2024. Sedation was administered using midazolam and/or propofol. After recovery from sedation, patients completed a questionnaire assessing preoperative anxiety, intraoperative memory, perceived treatment duration, mouth-opening discomfort, and overall satisfaction using an 11-point numerical rating scale (NRS). Satisfaction scores were categorized into low- (0-5) and high- (6-10) groups. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify associated factors. Among 639 eligible patients, 316 were included in the final analysis. Overall satisfaction with intravenous sedation was high (mean NRS score: 8.03 ± 2.74). Multivariable analysis identified three independent factors associated with lower satisfaction: lower preoperative anxiety, longer treatment time, and sedation performed for systemic disease management. Intravenous sedation maintained at the level of conscious sedation achieved high patient satisfaction during dental procedures. Lower preoperative anxiety, prolonged treatment time, and sedation for systemic disease management were associated with reduced satisfaction. These findings highlight the importance of appropriate case selection and ensuring patient understanding of sedation indications to improve satisfaction.

title: Exploring the porphyrin scaffold: promising prospects in the development of novel acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.
journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder marked by memory loss and cognitive decline. While no cure exists, inhibiting acetylcholinesterase (AChE) slows disease progression, making it a key therapeutic target. Porphyrin (Por) derivatives, though common in photodynamic therapy, have been rarely studied as AChE inhibitors. This study advances the development of free-base Por (H2Por 1-6), and zinc(II) Por (ZnPor 1a, 2a, 5a) as potential AChE inhibitors. Four molecules (H2Por 1, 2, 2a, 3) showed promising activities against AChE (IC50: 0.76-10.69 µM), being inactive against butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE, IC50 > 25 µM), with H2Por 2 demonstrating the highest potency (IC50 = 0.76 ± 0.11 µM) and selectivity (SI > 32.89). Furthermore, molecular docking studies provided comprehensive insights into the interactions between these compounds and AChE, supporting the observed biological activity. These findings enhance our understanding of structure-inhibition relationships, paving the way for Por-based AChE inhibitors in the treatment of AD.

title: 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: pilot study with fibroblast profiling.
abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is overexpressed on cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), driving an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We report a prospective study integrating ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET-CT with ex vivo CAF subset profiling in treatment-naïve NSCLC. 15 patients underwent 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT alongside standard-of-care imaging (Cohort 1: five surgical candidates; Cohort 2: ten advanced-disease patients). Standardised uptake values (SUV) were derived from primary tumour, lymph nodes, mediastinal blood pool (MBP), background lung and metastatic deposits. Plasma collagen remodelling biomarkers (PRO-C3, C3M, C3F, PRO-C11) were measured in 13 patients. Fresh tumour and adjacent non-cancerous lung tissue were samples following surgical resection (n = 5) to allow for CAF subset identification by flow cytometry. 68Ga-FAPI PET demonstrated avid uptake in all primary tumours (SUVmax 3.97-14.01; mean 9.67 ± 2.84) with low background lung signal (SUVmean mean 0.68 ± 0.28; range 0.30-1.27), yielding good tumour-to-background ratios (TBR mean 16.88 ± 9.85; range 8.07-40). Compared with 18F-FDG PET-CT, 68Ga-FAPI upstaged two patients (previously undetected bone and retro-orbital metastases), but demonstrated discordant (negative 68Ga-FAPI) nodal signal in two further patients. Plasma collagen biomarkers were measurable but did not correlate significantly with 68Ga-FAPI SUV (Spearman r ≤ 0.44 for all markers). FAP high CAF subsets (S1 + S5) were higher in tumour compared with matched normal lung and CAF S5 correlates with SUVmax (r = 0.90, p = 0.04). 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT is feasible and well-tolerated in NSCLC, provides complementary staging information to FDG PET-CT, and reflects tumour FAP biology as evidenced by ex vivo CAF subset enrichment. ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET-CT provides complementary staging information to ¹⁸F-FDG PET-CT in treatment-naïve NSCLC and is shown to reflect intratumoral FAP biology directly. This prospective pilot study provides preliminary evidence that ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-46 PET-CT may act as a non-invasive marker of the fibroblast-rich tumour microenvironment in NSCLC, which requires confirmation in larger cohorts.

title: Developmental site type, larval productivity, and insecticide susceptibility of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
abstract: Arboviral diseases, including dengue and chikungunya, are increasing in sub-Saharan Africa. This study assessed Aedes aegypti larval productivity across three container types and examined associations with abiotic parameters and insecticide resistance patterns in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. From July to September 2024, a semi-field experiment was conducted at the Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme. Tires, terracotta jars, and buckets were exposed outdoors for natural colonization. Larval abundance and six abiotic parameters (pH, temperature, salinity, conductivity, total dissolved solids, and redox potential) were recorded over 11 rounds. Susceptibility bioassays were performed on emerging Ae. aegypti adults using deltamethrin (0.03%), bendiocarb (0.2%), and malathion (1.5%). A total of 14,020 larvae were collected, of which 93.13% were Ae. aegypti. Tires (mean = 83.3 ± 10.8 larvae/container) and terracotta jars (mean = 50.7 ± 7.4 larvae/container) harbored significantly more larvae than buckets (mean = 22.5 ± 3.3 larvae/container); tires and jars did not differ significantly. Generalized linear mixed model analysis showed no significant effect of abiotic parameters, while container type was strongly associated with abundance. Ae. aegypti populations were resistant to deltamethrin in all container types (mortality 5.2%-17.9%) and to malathion in both tested container types (mortality 88.4%-88.8%). For bendiocarb, populations were resistant in plastic buckets (85.3% mortality), showed suspected resistance in tires (91.6%), and were susceptible in terracotta jars (98.6%). Vector control should prioritize the management of tires and terracotta jars, and widespread pyrethroid resistance highlights the need for alternative tools.

title: Classic psychedelics and the neuroendocrine system: A systematic review of human studies.
abstract: Classic psychedelics such as lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), psilocybin, mescaline, N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT), and ayahuasca exert profound psychological and physiological effects primarily through 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) 2A receptor activation. Beyond their well-described subjective effects, these substances also modulate neuroendocrine function, particularly hormones involved in stress regulation, homeostasis, and social behavior. Despite growing therapeutic interest, endocrine effects remain understudied. Electronic searches of three databases (PubMed, LILACS, Cochrane, and Web of Science) were conducted to identify studies from January 1, 1990, to July 17, 2026. Inclusion criteria were applied to select studies that investigated the neuroendocrine responses to classic psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, mescaline, and DMT/ayahuasca). We followed the PRISMA guidelines for data collection. Extracted variables included substance, dose, sample characteristics, timing of hormonal sampling, and reported effects on hormones. CRD420251052909. Nineteen studies met eligibility criteria. Across studies, the most consistent endocrine finding was a transient, dose-dependent increase in cortisol and, when measured, adrenocorticotropic hormone. This effect was observed following intravenous DMT, oral ayahuasca, psilocybin, and LSD. Prolactin elevations were similarly observed across psychedelics, whereas growth hormone responses were variable. Oxytocin increases were reported following LSD, mescaline, and, under specific administration conditions, DMT, although findings were less consistent than those observed for cortisol and prolactin. Thyroid-stimulating hormone, dehydroepiandrosterone, and circulating steroids were assessed in only a limited number of studies. Classic psychedelics induce acute neuroendocrine changes, with the most consistent evidence involving serotonergic-mediated activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, increasing cortisol levels. Evidence for other hormones remains variable or limited, highlighting the need for further controlled studies to clarify the mechanisms and clinical relevance of these responses.

title: Executive functioning in autistic young adults and those who have lost the autism diagnosis.
journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society : JINS
abstract: When individuals with an autism diagnosis lose that diagnosis, many questions remain about their history and current functioning. The Loss of Autism Diagnosis (LAD) outcome is associated with early, intense behavioral intervention, rapid response to intervention, and milder early autism features and developmental delays. This study probed for impairments in executive function (EF) in young adult LAD individuals relative to autistic and neurotypical peers, either in cognition or in everyday life, as well as any reemergence of autism features. Participants (mean age 22 years) included 29 individuals with a current autism diagnosis (AUT), 26 individuals who lost the AUT diagnosis (LAD), and 32 neurotypical controls (NT); groups did not differ on age, sex, and verbal or nonverbal functioning. Participants completed several measures of EF, and their parents reported on their EF via a standardized questionnaire. Findings indicated that LAD individuals in early adulthood maintained their lack of autism features and had EFs in cognition and in everyday life similar to those of neurotypical controls. In addition, autistic young adults with cognitive ability in the typical range showed that in everyday life, their EFs continued to fall below that of cognitively similar neurotypical and LAD individuals, especially in the domain of attention shifting. The challenges of the transition to adulthood did not appear to contribute to the reemergence of autism features or EF difficulties in LAD; however, many autistic young adults with age-typical cognitive abilities continued to show difficulties with some aspects of EF in everyday life.

title: Patterns of Methamphetamine Initiation, Use, and Treatment Experiences Among People With HIV: A Rapid Qualitative Analysis.
journal: Journal of the International Association of Providers of AIDS Care
abstract: BackgroundMethamphetamine use is common among people with HIV (PWH), yet HIV providers have limited guidance on how methamphetamine use evolves or how existing treatments meet patients' needs. We examined methamphetamine use trajectories and treatment experiences among PWH.MethodsFifteen PWH with moderate-to-high methamphetamine involvement were recruited from an academic HIV clinic. Semi-structured interviews (2021-2024) were analyzed using rapid qualitative analysis guided by the PARRQA framework.ResultsMethamphetamine use typically began through sexual partners or friends, escalated from occasional to weekly or daily use, and alternated with prolonged sobriety. Use was primarily sexualized, although some participants used methamphetamine to cope with stress. Participants valued treatment-related social connection and learning but reported limited support for harm-reduction goals.ConclusionMethamphetamine use among PWH followed a largely sexualized, escalating trajectory inadequately addressed by existing services. Integrating harm-reduction-oriented, chemsex-informed care into HIV settings may improve substance use and HIV outcomes.

title: Uniform Dataset 3 Neuropsychological Battery: A Czech Normative Study of a Battery Assessing Cognitive Functioning in Older Adults.
abstract: The Uniform Dataset Neuropsychological Battery, version 3 (UDSNB 3), is a comprehensive, nonproprietary tool designed to assess cognitive domains relevant to neurodegenerative disorders, particularly Alzheimer's disease. This study aimed to establish Czech norms for the UDSNB 3, including the Lewy body disease module, using continuous norming methods. A normative sample of 171 cognitively healthy adults aged 50-95 years was recruited. Participants completed the Czech adaptation of the UDSNB 3. Continuous norming was performed using a semi-parametric approach. Education and age effects were examined, and selected scores were compared with previous Czech normative studies. Cognitive performance generally declined with age across measures. Compared to previous Czech normative studies, differences were small and inconsistent across tests. The present study provides the first Czech normative data for UDSNB 3 using a continuous norming approach, supporting its clinical applicability. Continuous norming appears to be a viable approach for developing norms in the context of countries with limited resources or smaller populations, where collecting large stratified samples of older adults can be difficult.

title: The Orexinergic System in Alzheimer's Disease: From Sleep Disruption to Accelerated Neurodegeneration.
abstract: Sleep-wake dysregulation is increasingly recognized as an early and clinically relevant feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD), with growing evidence supporting a bidirectional relationship between disturbed sleep and AD pathophysiology. Sleep fragmentation and reduced slow-wave and REM sleep may contribute to amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation by increasing Aβ production during wakefulness and diminishing glymphatic clearance during sleep, while emerging amyloid pathology can further disrupt sleep architecture and circadian sleep-wake rhythm, reinforcing a feed-forward cycle. Within this framework, the orexinergic system, centered in the hypothalamus and crucial for arousal and sleep-wake stability, has been implicated as a mechanistic link between hyperarousal, impaired sleep consolidation, and altered amyloid dynamics. Preclinical studies suggested that orexin-A signaling can exacerbate Aβ and tau pathology and impair synaptic function, whereas biomarker studies reported high cerebrospinal fluid orexin-A levels in mild cognitive impairment and dementia due to AD. These observations raise the hypothesis that targeting orexin signaling and improving sleep may represent actionable strategies within the AD continuum. Clinical evidence indicates that behavioral and pharmacological interventions can improve sleep in at-risk populations, yet robust proof of disease-modifying effects on AD biomarkers or clinical progression remains limited. Ongoing trials of dual orexin receptor antagonists may clarify whether sustained modulation of sleep-wake regulation can influence AD-related biology beyond symptomatic sleep benefits.

title: Anorexia Nervosa, Voice-Hearing Experiences, and Risk of Misdiagnosis: A Scoping Review.
journal: The Journal of nervous and mental disease
abstract: To characterize the psychopathological features of hallucinations in anorexia nervosa (AN), compare them with the phenomenology of the anorexic voice (AV), and examine therapeutic interventions. We conducted a scoping review to identify studies examining hallucinations and the AV in AN. Nineteen studies were included. Both hallucinations and AV were described as self-critical, commanding, and commenting on eating attitudes and body shape. When reported, hallucinations were externally located, whereas, surprisingly, the location of the AV was not explicitly assessed in most studies. All patients with hallucinations were treated with antipsychotics, with marked improvement. Hallucinations and the AV show remarkable similarities that outweigh their differences. Potentially relevant features for distinguishing them (location, insight, co-occurring psychotic symptoms) were poorly examined in studies of the AV, limiting the identification of meaningful differences. Clear discrimination appears relevant for therapeutic implications, as hallucinations and the AV seem to follow different treatment pathways.

title: Neuron-tumor network integration drives glioma progression through synaptic coupling, metabolic reprogramming, and neuroimmune remodeling.
journal: Journal of neuropathology and experimental neurology
abstract: Traditionally regarded as space-occupying lesions, gliomas, particularly glioblastoma, are increasingly recognized as tumors that interact extensively with surrounding neural circuits. Glioma cells establish functional excitatory synapses with neurons and form interconnected networks through tumor microtubes, facilitating electrical integration and intercellular communication. They also coopt activity-dependent neuronal paracrine factors to promote proliferation and exploit neurotransmitter signaling and ion channels to sustain a hyperexcitable tumor microenvironment. Beyond neuronal signaling, gliomas engage in metabolic interactions with surrounding cells, including astrocyte-to-glioma mitochondrial transfer, macrophage-mediated recycling of myelin-derived lipids, and tumor-induced astrocyte reprogramming. These processes are closely associated with immunosuppressive signaling. Together, these mechanisms may establish self-reinforcing neuron-tumor feedback loops that remodel neural circuits and contribute to epilepsy, cognitive decline, and therapeutic resistance in patients. This review synthesizes current evidence across 4 interconnected dimensions: physical connectivity, chemical signaling hijacking, metabolic reprogramming, and neuroimmune remodeling. Building on these findings, we propose a hypothesis-generating model linking neural network integration, altered metabolic resource exchange, and immunosuppressive niches. The model distinguishes experimentally supported findings from proposed feedback relationships, identifies testable predictions, and provides a rationale for organizing network-oriented therapeutic strategies according to the tumor-host interactions they target while considering the preservation of normal brain function.

title: Assessing the role of single human chromosome 21 gene orthologues on amyloid-β toxicity in fly models.
abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome face a high risk of early-onset Alzheimer's disease. While an additional copy of the amyloid beta precursor protein gene (APP) is a primary trigger, other human chromosome 21 (Hsa21) genes are known to modulate amyloid-β1-42 (Aβ42) pathology and response. However, the relative impact of single genes during early neurodevelopment or in adult neurons remains unclear. To systematically evaluate the contribution of single gene effects, we overexpressed conserved Hsa21 Drosophila orthologues in an adult-restricted model of Aβ42 adult locomotor toxicity and found no single gene was able to modulate this biology. To evaluate developmental effects, we expressed these Hsa21 orthologues in the developing fly eye. We found that overexpression of the Hsa21 orthologues Pten/TPTE, Sik2/SIK1, plp/PCNT, pnt/ETS2 and O-fut2/POFUT2 significantly exacerbated Aβ42-induced rough eye phenotypes. Crucially, overexpression of pnt and O-fut2 was sufficient to drive severe neurodegeneration even in the absence of Aβ42. Our findings suggest that direct modulation of Aβ42 adult locomotor toxicity downstream of APP by single Hsa21 orthologues in adult neurons is limited in our model. Instead, overexpression of genes such as pnt/ETS2 and O-fut2/POFUT2 can disrupt early neurodevelopment, which may establish long-lasting vulnerabilities that impact on the later effect of Aβ42, underscoring the critical role of early brain development in later Down Syndrome Alzheimer's disease progression.

title: Non-Invasive Magnetic Resonance Imaging After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Scoping Review of DTI-ALPS and Enlarged Perivascular Space Findings.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
abstract: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) may lead to a buildup of neurotoxic metabolites in the brain that require clearance by the glymphatic system. Non-invasive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) methods such as the diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index and enlarged perivascular space (ePVS) quantification post-mTBI are being increasingly adopted despite an incomplete understanding of the biological limitations and methodological considerations of these techniques. To synthesize the current literature and identify knowledge gaps, a comprehensive search was performed using PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials. Human studies written in English between 2000 and 2025 were included, resulting in 18 studies in the final sample. Extracted data included: study design and population, number of participants, time from injury, MRI method, and results. PRISMA reporting guidelines for scoping reviews were followed. Included studies were heterogeneous in study design, choice of study population, time from injury to MRI scan, confounders controlled for, and study results. Decreases in the DTI-ALPS index were reported in studies including mixed injury severities and, in some studies limited to mTBI, while other mTBI-only studies reported increases or no change. ePVS findings were also heterogeneous, with studies reporting either no group differences or higher ePVS measures in injured participants. This scoping review identified three studies that included both DTI-ALPS index and ePVS quantification and determined that these measures may assess distinct biological processes. These results highlight the need for multiparametric, standardized MRI investigations of the glymphatic system post-mTBI.

title: Regulatory Roles of Reactive Nitrogen Species During Gecko Tail Regeneration: Insights From the Nitrosoproteome and Functional Perturbations.
journal: Wound repair and regeneration : official publication of the Wound Healing Society [and] the European Tissue Repair Society
abstract: Injury or disease conditions cause inflammation, resulting in oxidative and nitrosative stress. Injury-induced inflammation is essential for blastema-mediated tissue regeneration, and although the role of oxidative stress is well established, the contribution of nitrosative stress remains poorly understood. The main contributors of nitrosative stress are reactive nitrogen species (RNS), such as nitric oxide and peroxynitrite. Nitric oxide is a crucial signalling molecule involved in protein S-nitrosylation, a post-translational modification essential for cellular signalling and redox regulation. Gecko tail regeneration provides an excellent model for studying blastema-mediated regeneration, and in this study, the proteome and nitrosoproteome of the regenerating tail 5 days post-autotomy were characterised using ESI-QTOF-MS. Functional perturbations with the NOS inhibitor L-NAME and the peroxynitrite decomposition catalyst FeTMPyP, followed by differential pentachrome staining for collagens and glycosaminoglycans, were performed to examine treatment-associated changes and explore the possible involvement of RNS in extracellular matrix organisation. A nitric oxide donor, sodium nitrite, and retinoic acid, a signalling molecule, were topically applied to amputated gecko limbs to explore their potential effects post-injury in a non-regenerating organ. The nitrosoproteome of the 5-day post-autotomy (dpa) tail identified candidate s-nitrosylated proteins annotated to extracellular matrix components, cell migration, and neuronal development, with inhibitor experiments suggesting a role for nitrosative stress in matrix organisation. Sodium nitrite appeared to promote cell proliferation but did not induce tissue regrowth, whereas retinoic acid was associated with partial tissue outgrowth comprising Schwann cells, nerve fibre, muscle and scales in the amputated gecko limb. The study provides a catalogue of S-nitrosylated proteins observed during gecko tail regeneration, identifies the association of reactive nitrogen species with ECM organisation and presents retinoic acid as a plausible inducer of partial regrowth in otherwise non-regenerating gecko limbs.

title: Schwann Cells Mount an Early Injury Response in Sarm1 Knockout Nerves, and Glial Sarm1 Loss Delays Axon Degeneration.
abstract: Schwann cells (SCs) transition into a Repair state after peripheral nerve injury, but their early injury response remains poorly understood. To characterize SC injury responses before axon fragmentation and in the absence of axonal SARM1 activity, we profiled WT and global Sarm1-knockout nerves within the first day after transection by single-nucleus RNA sequencing. We observed a substantial transcriptional injury response, enrichment of a putative intermediate SC state, and increased oxidative phosphorylation gene expression across injured SC states. These genotype-associated differences may reflect the absence of SARM1-dependent axonal signals, Sarm1 loss within SCs, or contributions from other cell types; they do not establish cell-autonomous control of the repair-state transition. We then asked whether glial Sarm1 influences axon degeneration when neuronal SARM1 is intact. We detect Sarm1 transcripts in SCs that increase after nerve injury. Reducing SC or glial Sarm1 delayed axon degeneration in co-cultures of Sarm1-knockout SCs with wild-type neurons, Sarm1 conditional knockout in Sox10 positive cells in mice, and Drosophila with pan-glial dSarm knockdown. Together, our findings characterize early SC injury states in nerves lacking SARM1-dependent axon degeneration and support a glial contribution to axon degeneration kinetics.

title: When Arousal Backfires: Pupillary Reactivity and Pain Catastrophizing Interact in Predicting Conditioned Pain Modulation.
abstract: Conditioned pain modulation (CPM) indexes descending pain inhibition, yet its psychophysical assessment is influenced by subjective and cognitive factors. Pupillometry provides an indirect marker of locus coeruleus-noradrenergic (LC-NE) activity, implicated in both arousal and pain modulation. We examined whether pupillary reactivity to a cold pressor test (CPT) predicted CPM and whether this relationship depended on pain catastrophizing. Fifty-five healthy, pain-free adults (56% male; mean age 28.1 years) completed the Pain Catastrophizing Scale (PCS). CPM was assessed as changes in heat (ΔHPT) and pressure (ΔPPT) pain thresholds before and after a 120-s CPT (10°C). Pupil diameter was recorded binocularly during the CPT; the area under the curve (AUC) of baseline-corrected, z-scored pupil size was the pupillometric index. Hierarchical linear regressions tested Pupil AUC, its interaction with standardized PCS and covariates (age, CPT pain intensity). A significant model emerged for ΔPPT (R2 = 0.354, p < 0.001), revealing an interaction between Pupil AUC and pain catastrophizing (β = 0.522, p < 0.001). Higher catastrophizing was associated with reduced inhibition, an association stronger in participants with greater pupillary reactivity and independent of CPT pain intensity. Age was also predictive. No associations emerged for ΔHPT. Pupillary reactivity did not directly predict CPM but interacted with pain catastrophizing in predicting pressure pain inhibition, independently of the perceived intensity of the conditioning stimulus.
